observations.fact: The U.S. Department of Commerce finalized an award to Texas Instruments of up to $1.61 billion in direct CHIPS Incentives funding supporting more than $18 billion of TI investment through the end of the decade across three new facilities in Texas and Utah; disbursement is tied to project milestones.

Commerce describes TI as a leading U.S. analog and embedded-processing manufacturer and states the projects are intended to expand domestic production of foundational current-generation and mature-node semiconductors used across electronic systems.

risks.risk: Award funding is milestone-dependent, so the government commitment does not by itself prove fab utilization, economic returns, or end-demand strength.

unknowns.unknown: Current fab utilization, incremental returns on the 300mm buildout, and current valuation remain for Council Alpha underwriting.
